edges.description: Collagen IX is an obligate heterotrimer of alpha-1, alpha-2 and alpha-3 chains, so losing one chain prevents assembly of the molecule.

nodes.description: The vitreous gel is hypoplastic with abnormal architecture. In recessive Stickler syndrome it is not assigned to the membranous or beaded categories used to subclassify the dominant forms.

nodes.description: Joint pain is uncommon and variable, in contrast with the dominant forms where it reaches 90% by age 40. One type IX patient with severe arthropathy has been reported, so the mild course is not universal.

nodes.description: Hearing loss is severe and near-universal, so audiological assessment and amplification are central to management. The literature's emphasis is on getting to the diagnosis early, because dual sensory impairment in a child is what the delay costs.

evidence.snippet: Although recessive SS is rare, early diagnosis would have a high impact for children with potentially dual sensory impairment, as well as identifying risk to future children.

nodes.description: Activities carrying a risk of ocular trauma are avoided because trauma can precipitate retinal detachment in an eye whose vitreous is already abnormal. This is the one piece of standard Stickler management that the type IX data does not qualify: the argument rests on the vitreous abnormality, which the type IX cohort confirms, rather than on the giant-tear risk, which it does not.

evidence.reference_title: Stickler Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Activities such as contact sports that may lead to traumatic retinal detachment.

evidence.reference_title: A loss of function mutation in the COL9A2 gene causes autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Affected family members were found to have a homozygous loss-of-function mutation in COL9A2, c.843_c.846 + 4del8.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal Recessive Stickler Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Usually inherited in a dominant fashion due to heterozygous pathogenic variants in the collagen genes COL2A1 and COL11A1, it can rarely be inherited in a recessive fashion from variants in COL9A1, COL9A2, and COL9A3, COL11A1, as well as the non-collagen genes LRP2, LOXL3 and GZF1.

nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants — frameshift, splice-disrupting deletion — abolish the alpha-2 chain of collagen IX. Reported alleles include c.843_846+4del8, which removes an exon-intron boundary, and c.1332del.

evidence.snippet: Affected family members were found to have a homozygous loss-of-function mutation in COL9A2, c.843_c.846 + 4del8.

nodes.description: Collagen IX loss in hyaline cartilage produces a markedly milder skeletal and orofacial phenotype than the dominant collagen II and XI Sticklers. Midface hypoplasia is present in a minority, arthropathy is uncommon and variable, and cleft palate — a defining feature of the collagen XI forms — has not been reported in a type IX patient at all. Short stature was described in the founding family.

evidence.reference_title: Retinal detachment in Type IX collagen recessive Stickler syndrome.
evidence.snippet: No patients had cleft palate, and 30.8% had midfacial hypoplasia.

evidence.reference_title: Retinal detachment in Type IX collagen recessive Stickler syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Arthropathy was uncommon but variable in manifestation.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal Recessive Stickler Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Cleft palate is associated with type XI collagen variants, as well as the non-collagen genes, but is so far unreported with type IX collagen variants.

nodes.description:
Prophylactic cryotherapy or laser retinopexy is standard in type 1 Stickler syndrome, where lifetime retinal detachment risk exceeds 50% and giant retinal tears dominate. The type IX cohort does not support transferring that policy: detachment was less frequent, through horseshoe tears, with no giant tears and no bilateral cases. The authors' conclusion is that prophylaxis should be offered case by case, specifically for the fellow eye of a patient who has already had a giant-tear detachment. This entry records the restriction rather than the intervention, because the restriction is the finding.
The restriction is not a claim that prophylaxis does not work. The pro-prophylaxis evidence base in Stickler syndrome generally is strong, and the review that makes that case names the missing piece itself: the cohort comparisons it rests on were done without molecular genetic sub-typing. The type IX cohort is what sub-typing looks like when it is done, so the two findings are consistent rather than opposed.

evidence.reference_title: Retinal detachment in Type IX collagen recessive Stickler syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Prophylactic retinopexy should only be offered case-by-case for fellow eyes of patients presenting with GRT detachments in their first eye.

evidence.snippet: Based on the current body of literature, there is extremely strong evidence from cohort comparison studies demonstrating the efficacy and safety of prophylactic retinopexy to reduce, but not eliminate, the risk of retinal detachment in Stickler syndrome patients.

evidence.reference_title: Prevention of Blindness in Stickler Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Variable case selection, absence of molecular genetic sub-typing and inconsistent treatment strategies have all contributed to the historic uncertainty regarding the safety and efficacy of prophylactic treatment.

nodes.description: Sensorineural hearing loss is near-universal and more severe than in the dominant forms, typically with a down-sloping high-frequency audiogram. The step from collagen IX loss to cochlear dysfunction is not mechanistically worked out in humans; what is established is the epidemiology, and it is strong enough that the literature recommends adding COL9A1, COL9A2 and COL9A3 to congenital hearing loss gene panels.

evidence.reference_title: Retinal detachment in Type IX collagen recessive Stickler syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Hearing loss was more prevalent (91.7%) than in dominant SS.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous Type IX collagen variants (COL9A1, COL9A2, and COL9A3) causing recessive Stickler syndrome-Expanding the phenotype.
evidence.snippet: We suggest that COL9A1, COL9A2, and COL9A3 be added to genetic screening panels for patients with congenital hearing loss.

nodes.description: Without the alpha-2 chain, functional collagen IX is not formed. Collagen IX is a FACIT collagen that sits on the surface of collagen II fibrils and mediates their interaction with the surrounding matrix, so its absence is felt wherever a collagen II fibril network has to be spaced and stabilised — principally the vitreous gel and hyaline cartilage.

evidence.reference_title: A loss of function mutation in the COL9A2 gene causes autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Together the data from the present study and the previous studies suggest that loss-of-function mutations in any of the collagen IX genes can cause autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome.

nodes.description: High myopia is present in essentially every reported patient and is usually the first ocular sign, accompanying congenital enlargement of the globe.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal Recessive Stickler Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: High myopia is near-universal, and sensorineural hearing loss is very common in patients with variants in genes for type IX or XI collagen

nodes.description: Midfacial hypoplasia is present in a minority and is subtle where it occurs — considerably milder than in the dominant Sticklers.

evidence.reference_title: Retinal detachment in Type IX collagen recessive Stickler syndrome.
evidence.snippet: No patients had cleft palate, and 30.8% had midfacial hypoplasia.

nodes.description: Retinal detachment occurs but at a much lower rate than in type 1 Stickler syndrome, and with a different mechanism: horseshoe tears rather than giant retinal tears, and no bilateral cases in the national cohort. This is the single most consequential difference between STL5 and the dominant forms, because giant-tear detachment is what prophylactic retinopexy exists to prevent.

evidence.reference_title: Retinal detachment in Type IX collagen recessive Stickler syndrome.
evidence.snippet: 15.4% of patients developed RD secondary to horseshoe retinal tears, with no cases of bilateral RD or giant retinal tears (GRTs).

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal Recessive Stickler Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Retinal detachment has occurred in 18% of all cases, and joint pain in 15%.

nodes.description: Surgical repair of established detachment, reported in a COL9A2 proband. Outcomes in Stickler syndrome are described as notably worse than detachment repair in the general population, which is the observation the prophylaxis argument is built on — so the poor-outcome figure belongs with the surgery rather than only with the prophylaxis debate.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome associated with homozygous mutations in the COL9A2 gene.
evidence.snippet: The proband was operated for retinal detachment and cataract in one eye.

evidence.reference_title: Prevention of Blindness in Stickler Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Although retinal detachment surgery in the general population has a high success rate, outcomes from surgical repair in Stickler syndrome patients are notoriously poor, providing a strong argument for prophylactic intervention.

nodes.description: Severe sensorineural hearing loss with a down-sloping audiogram, more prevalent and more severe than in dominant Stickler syndrome. It is the feature most likely to bring a child to attention first.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome associated with homozygous mutations in the COL9A2 gene.
evidence.snippet: Both brothers have severe sensorineural hearing loss with down-sloping audiograms but only subtle midface hypoplasia and no, or mild joint problems.

nodes.description: The vitreous is hypoplastic with abnormal architecture, and the globe is enlarged with high axial myopia. Unlike the dominant forms, which each have a characteristic membranous or beaded vitreous phenotype, the type IX vitreous is described simply as hypoplastic and abnormal. Retinal function is measurably reduced on electroretinography even where the macula looks structurally normal, which is the finding that explains visual acuity loss in these patients without retinal complications.

evidence.snippet: All patients were highly myopic with congenital megalophthalmos and abnormal, hypoplastic vitreous gel

evidence.snippet: Moreover, we demonstrate reduced macular and overall retinal function explaining the reduced visual acuity in patients with Stickler syndrome also without retinal complications.

Homozygous in the founding family. An eight-base deletion spanning an exon-intron boundary, reported as loss of function.
